easy.def: A word that shows the place or time of something.
examples: I am at school.
We eat lunch at noon.
She is at the door.

more.def: A word used to show a place or a point in time, or the thing that someone aims or looks toward.
examples: The bus arrives at the corner of Main Street at eight o'clock.
She smiled at the baby sleeping in the stroller.
We stayed at my grandmother's house for the weekend.

easy.def: A person who plays sports very well.
examples: The athlete ran fast.
She is an athlete.
The athlete won a medal.

more.def: A person who is trained and skilled at sports or games that need strength and speed.
examples: The athlete trained every day.
She is an athlete who runs marathons.
The athletes walked into the stadium.

easy.def: Good at sports or strong and fit.
examples: She is very athletic.
He has an athletic body.
We have athletic shoes.

more.def: Having to do with sports, or strong and good at sports.
examples: She is very athletic and plays three sports.
The athletic shoes had thick soles for running.
He is tall and athletic, and he can jump very high.

easy.def: The air around the earth.
examples: Rockets fly through the atmosphere.
The atmosphere has oxygen.
The atmosphere is thin high up.

more.def: The layer of air and gases that surrounds a planet.
examples: The rocket flew up through the atmosphere.
The earth's atmosphere has the air we breathe.
The atmosphere gets thinner as you go higher.

easy.def: The feeling of a place.
examples: The party had a happy atmosphere.
The atmosphere was calm.
The restaurant has a cozy atmosphere.

more.def: The mood or feeling that a place has.
examples: The party had a happy, friendly atmosphere.
The library has a calm atmosphere.
The cafe has a cozy atmosphere.

easy.def: The tiniest part of anything that is still that kind of thing.
examples: Everything is made of atoms.
An atom is too small to see.
Water is made of atoms.

more.def: One of the very tiny building blocks that everything is made of.
examples: Everything in the world is made of atoms too small to see.
A water molecule has two atoms of hydrogen and one of oxygen.
Scientists use special tools to study how atoms behave.

easy.def: Having to do with atoms.
examples: An atomic scientist.
The atomic clock is exact.
An atomic bomb.

more.def: Having to do with atoms, the tiny parts that everything is made of.
examples: The scientist studied atomic structure.
An atomic clock keeps very exact time.
Atomic energy comes from atoms.

easy.def: On top of.
examples: The cat sat atop the wall.
A flag flew atop the pole.
He stood atop the hill.

more.def: On the top of something.
examples: The cat sat atop the fence.
A flag flew atop the tower.
He stood atop the hill and looked around.

easy.def: To fasten one thing to another.
examples: Attach the string to the kite.
I attached the tag.
She attached a note.

more.def: To join or fix one thing to another.
examples: I attached the string to the kite.
She attached a note to the gift.
Attach the photo to the page with tape.

easy.def: To start a fight against someone.
examples: The soldiers attacked the fort.
A bee may attack if it is afraid.
The fox attacked the henhouse.

more.def: To use force to hurt or fight against a person, animal or place.
examples: Bees may attack if you disturb their nest.
The knights attacked the castle in the old story.
Some sharks attack only when they are scared.

easy.def: A try to hurt someone with force.
examples: The attack on the castle failed.
A bee's attack can hurt.
The fox ran away after the attack.

more.def: An act of using force to hurt or fight against someone.
examples: The castle held out against the attack.
The fox made an attack on the henhouse, but the dog barked.
Wasps may make an attack if you bump their nest.

easy.def: A try to do something.
examples: It was my first attempt to skate.
Her attempt to jump the fence failed.
He made an attempt to cook.

more.def: An effort to do something, especially something hard.
examples: After three attempts, she finally rode the bike without help.
The climbers made an attempt to reach the top.
His attempt to build the tower in one try did not work.

easy.def: To try to do something.
examples: I will attempt to read the book.
She attempted a high jump.
They attempted to cross the stream.

more.def: To try to do something, often something that is hard.
examples: The swimmer attempted to cross the lake.
He attempted to fix the bike on his own.
Scientists attempted the experiment many times.

easy.def: To go to a place and be there.
examples: I attend school.
We will attend the party.
She attended the show.

more.def: To be present at an event or place, such as a school or meeting.
examples: I attend a school near my home.
The whole family attended the wedding.
Hundreds of people attended the parade.

easy.def: A person whose job is to help people in a place.
examples: The flight attendant gave us snacks.
A pool attendant watched us.
The parking attendant waved.

more.def: A person who is employed to help or serve people in a certain place.
examples: The flight attendant gave us juice and peanuts.
A pool attendant watched the children swim.
The parking attendant showed us where to leave the car.

easy.def: Looking and listening with care.
examples: Please pay attention to the teacher.
The clown got our attention with a horn.
Babies need a lot of attention.

more.def: Careful watching, listening, or thinking about something.
examples: The loud noise caught the attention of the whole class.
Pay attention to the signs when you cross the street.
The puppy barked to get its owner's attention.

easy.def: The space under the roof of a house.
examples: The toys are in the attic.
The attic is dusty.
We climbed to the attic.

more.def: The space or room just under the roof of a house.
examples: Old boxes are stored in the attic.
The attic was dusty and warm.
We found a trunk in the attic.

easy.def: The way you think and feel about something.
examples: She has a good attitude.
He has a happy attitude.
Keep a cheerful attitude.

more.def: The way you think, feel and act about something or someone.
examples: A positive attitude can help you learn new things.
His bad attitude made the game less fun.
Our coach likes a player with a hard-working attitude.

easy.def: A lawyer.
examples: The attorney spoke in court.
My aunt is an attorney.
The attorney helped the family.

more.def: A lawyer, a person trained to speak for others in court.
examples: The attorney spoke to the judge.
Her attorney explained the rules.
An attorney helped the family sign the papers.

easy.def: To pull something closer.
examples: A magnet attracts metal.
Flowers attract bees.
Bright colors attract birds.

more.def: To draw something or someone closer, or to make them interested.
examples: A magnet attracts small pieces of metal.
Bright flowers attract bees and butterflies.
The circus attracted a big crowd.

easy.def: Something people want to see or do.
examples: The zoo is an attraction.
The park has many attractions.
The main attraction is the roller coaster.

more.def: Something that people find interesting and want to visit or see.
examples: The zoo is the main attraction in town.
The park has many attractions for kids.
The roller coaster is the biggest attraction.

easy.def: A pull toward something.
examples: The magnet has attraction.
The attraction of the moon pulls the tide.
The attraction is strong.

more.def: A force that pulls one thing toward another.
examples: A magnet has an attraction for iron.
The moon's attraction causes the tides.
The attraction between the two magnets was strong.

easy.def: Nice to look at.
examples: The house is attractive.
She wore an attractive dress.
The garden was attractive.

more.def: Pleasing to look at, or interesting enough to catch your attention.
examples: The shop had an attractive window full of toys.
An attractive poster drew people to the fair.
The park is an attractive place to have lunch.
